verdicts.reason: ADR-0031 core decision (no production restore tool in phase one) is sound and honest, and boundary, minimality, format and traceability all pass; but the permission invariant 'execution identity must not write Journal/keyring/lock/Store binding' is absent from design.md:3862 and has no enforcement mechanism (no DB role/GRANT/schema scope) anywhere in ADR-0031, while design.md:3864 hands the target DSN to the executor and design.md:3866 has root writing binding/audit into the same Store. gap-map section 2.5 requires a security review PASS, so neither design nor security can be concluded PASS.

items.summary: ADR-0031 forbids the execution identity from writing Journal/keyring/lock/Store binding, but design.md:3862 only forbids transmission, design.md:3864 gives the executor the target DSN, design.md:3866 has root writing binding/audit into the same Store, and ADR-0031 contains no GRANT, DB role or schema-scope restriction; the release condition merely defers an approved permission matrix. ADR adoption record :1044 also claims :3862 already fixes the root permission boundary.
items.impact: Production remains closed (recoveryClosedRestoreDriver refuses Prepare/Replace/VerifyRestored), so no live exposure; but the permission/ACL part of gap-map section 2.5 cannot be objectively verified, so security review cannot be PASS and design cannot be PASS.
items.requiredFix: Add to design.md:3862 the write-side negative matrix plus an enforcement mechanism (DB role limited to the application schema, or restore into an isolated database then a root-controlled switch, or explicit exclusion of recovery Store/Journal schema from the artifact); add a negative verification gate to ADR section 8 (executor credentials writing Journal/keyring/lock/Store binding must fail); clarify that 'must not write Store binding' means producing no authoritative binding/audit rows and define how root re-establishes and checks them after replacement; make :1044 match the design text.

items.summary: design.md:3862 omits three ADR negatives: tool-supplier self-approval ban, root must not substitute execution/enter shell/replay, and no network beyond the target connection.
items.impact: ADR stays authoritative and production is closed, so this is not blocking alone; an implementer reading only the design could miss egress restriction and the supplier self-approval ban.
items.requiredFix: Sync the three negatives into design.md:3862, preferably in the same revision as RV-01.

items.summary: ADR-0031 and design scope the closed state to the production enter/resume DB replacement, while ADR-0030:926 says production recovery enter/install keep returning closed.
items.impact: Combined state is still fully closed (ADR-0030 unchanged, design :3892 keeps enter/install closed without an anchor), but a reader of ADR-0031 alone could infer enter outside DB replacement is available.
items.requiredFix: Unify the wording or add an explicit ADR-0030 cross-reference; may be carried into D04 or a later revision.

items.summary: Author report says line 83 kept its first 744 characters unchanged; measured common prefix is 1184 characters and the whole before text is a prefix, with a 462-character / 760-byte tail appended.
items.impact: Does not change the reviewed files; the reviewer's own reverse reconstruction passed. Only the evidence arithmetic is inconsistent.
items.requiredFix: Change 744 to 1184 and state 'whole before text retained, 462 characters / 760 bytes appended'.

items.summary: No POSIX identity-switch mechanism is specified; su/sudo or script wrappers would contradict 'no shell, no extra argv'.
items.impact: Assembly could pick a mechanism that violates the isolation contract.
items.requiredFix: Fix fork + setgroups/setgid/setuid + exec (or an approved single launcher) in D04 or the formal implementation task, and forbid su/sudo-style wrapping.
